text: If your girlfriend tells you, who are you to tell me anything? Is that enough ground to end the relationship? Let's go to the question from one of my subscribers. Hey bro! First of all, I just want to say that I really like your videos. I respect your mindset and the way you explain things, which is why I am asking you for honest advice. I am currently working in London for 10 days. While I was away, my girlfriend went out to a club on Christmas with her friends. She was wearing a very short dress, which honestly felt like too much for me. I didn't tell her what she should wear, I just said it made me uncomfortable. She put a blazer on, but the dress was still very short, so nothing really changed. When I tried to explain how I felt, she started mocking me, saying things like I am from Afghanistan and asking who I am to tell her anything. That really bothered me, especially because I was trying to communicate calmly and respectfully. Another issue is social media and messaging. When I say delivering, I mean that sometimes when she sends me a message, I don't reply immediately because I am busy with training or other responsibilities. She keeps complaining about that, even though I am not ignoring her on purpose, I am just genuinely busy at times. She also had a male friend from her class. He was not into her, they just go to the same class. But he got angry at her because she didn't want to go out with him anymore. She stopped hanging out with him because of me, but I never asked her to do that. It was her own decision. I respect that, but in my opinion that's just the bare minimum in a relationship. Another thing that bothered me is that she still had videos of her ex on her phone for the first months of our relationship, and I had to point it out to her. She also goes to clubs very often, but to be fair, I do too, so I can't really blame her for that. We love each other, and I truly care about her. That is why I am trying to understand whether I am overreacting or if my boundaries are reasonable. I'd really appreciate your honest opinion on this situation, what do you think, and what would you do if you were in my place. Thanks a lot for your time, Ilyas. And this was my answer. Hey man, thanks for your question. There is quite a bit to unpack here, and many of the things I say you probably wouldn't like. But it is an ugly truth. First, you told your girlfriend that her wearing a short dress to a club makes you uncomfortable, but she just dismissed it. I would probably even start with why she goes to a club without you. Is it really okay with you? Anyways, this shows lack of empathy, lack of care towards you, and honestly, lack of respect. Then when you try to talk to her, instead of trying to compromise, find a middle ground, understand your point, she mocks you. Is that really a partner you want to have by your side and can trust? Second, she doesn't understand that you can be busy, working, and training. Does she work herself? From an experience, I can say that girls who never worked themselves, who just enjoy life because someone else gives them money, parents, boyfriend, etc. They do not understand what it is to be busy, to be working hard, to be earning money. And these girls are normally not suitable for relationships. Moreover, notice when something bothers you, she just dismisses it and mocks you. But when something bothers her, she is ready to talk about it seriously. Where is the reciprocity? Relationships should work both ways. You give and you receive. Once again, is that a partner you want to have by your side? The male friend part is fine. Well, I'm saying this because she cut him off. But I wouldn't be surprised that she stopped talking to him not because of you, but because she lost interest or the guy said or did something. The video of an ex is also a problem. The fact that you had to tell her that already speaks volumes. Once again, lack of empathy, lack of care about what do you feel, whether you are bothered by it or not. The clubbing part. As a person who used to party quite a bit, I don't quite understand why do you need to go clubbing if in a relationship. Don't you have other ways how to spend your weekend? I mean, I get it, once in a while. It doesn't matter if, for example, a friend decided to celebrate birthday at a club, but you do you generally speaking in a relationship. If you expect your partner to behave a certain way, you should live up to that standard yourself. So I would say it is normal for you and your girlfriend not to go to parties or clubs without each other. So this one, I would say a red flag both on your and your girlfriend's part. Overall, if I be honest, I do not think you have a healthy relationship. And since you already tried to talk to your girlfriend and it didn't work out, I don't think you guys have a good future. Even one of the red flags above are enough to end the relationship. But in your case, you have three or four. And since there is probably more to your relationship than what you wrote, there are also more red flags. So my suggestion would be to end the relationship, try to live solo for some time, enjoy your time in London, work on your career, do sports, have hobbies, start going on a date with other women. You probably would be much happier that way.
